headline_html: At a 15.5% host fee, a $200 night pays you $169, not $194
fix: Adding the points to your price still leaves you short. Divide the payout you want by 0.845, then check it against your market.
footer: Written by a finance executive who runs two Superhost rentals
voice_lines: Airbnb moved most hosts to a fifteen and a half percent host fee. Here is what it does to a two hundred dollar night.
At the old three percent fee, you kept one ninety four. At fifteen and a half, the same night pays one sixty nine.
Most hosts raise the price twelve and a half percent, to two twenty five. That still only pays one ninety.
The fix is division. Take the payout you want and divide by point eight four five. That's two thirty.
Then check it against your market. The full pricing worksheet is linked in the description.
